entry.title: Streaming Toward Ai Agent Behavior Research A Behavioral Science Approach To Machine Decis 76A7521Eac
entry.summary: Toward AI Agent Behavior Research identifies a lack of systematic frameworks for understanding how AI agents make decisions. This broadens Kaal's longitudinal judicial-AI evidence gap to agent-decision behavior more generally. The abstract proposition does not measure decision quality, backlog effects, trust, or long-term outcomes.

entry.title: Streaming Discrete Judgment Intermediate Multi Agent Architecture For Global Ai Oversight 8231Bcebfa
entry.summary: Discrete Judgment Intermediate states that its AI-oversight architecture combines universal principles with jurisdictional overlays. This independently corresponds to Kaal's hybrid universal-baseline and locally tailored governance structure. The abstract does not establish that the overlays preserve innovation or outperform harmonized substantive rules.

entry.title: Streaming Decentralized Multi Agent Reinforcement Learning Based On Best Response Policies C3Ddbdb049
entry.summary: Decentralized multi-agent reinforcement learning based on best-response policies reports that most studies use fully centralized learning to ease transfer from single-agent systems. This extends Kaal's centralization critique beyond federated-learning aggregators by identifying ease of methodological transfer as another centralization pressure. The abstract does not establish the communication-load or vulnerability effects Kaal identifies.

entry.title: Streaming The Verifiable Responsible Agent Framework Making Ai Agents Liable For Their Mis 6Bf1150496
entry.summary: The Verifiable Responsible Agent Framework states that loss caused by an autonomous AI agent may leave no liable subject because the model is not a legal person and the deploying operator may be too remote for liability. This independently agrees with Kaal's legal-personality gap and adds operator remoteness as a compensation obstacle. The abstract does not resolve liability allocation.

entry.title: Streaming Sovereign Agent Identity The Case For Individual Presence In Agentic Ai Ecosyste 22557Aec60
entry.summary: Sovereign Agent Identity identifies an infrastructure asymmetry: institutions have agentic systems participating in consequential decisions, while affected individuals lack equivalent agentic presence or a way to be addressed as participants rather than subjects. This supplies an independent access problem to which Kaal's self-sovereign identity mechanism is responsive. The abstract does not show that verifiable credentials alone cure the broader imbalance.

entry.title: Streaming Agentledger A Causal Ledger Architecture For Auditable Ai Agent Actions A93Fbfc510
entry.summary: AgentLedger states that the reasoning chain producing an AI-agent action is simply gone in the deployment baseline it addresses. This qualifies Kaal's real-time attestation claim by limiting it to architectures that actually retain and attest decision traces. The abstract proposition does not show that such attestation is impossible.

entry.title: Streaming Agentledger A Causal Ledger Architecture For Auditable Ai Agent Actions 95Da965B29
entry.summary: AgentLedger states that AI agents are being deployed in consequential settings faster than governance tools are being built. This independently corresponds to Kaal's governance-capability lag for evolving and deployed AI. The abstract does not establish that every legacy governance system lacks every required tool.

entry.title: Streaming Securing Brand Trust And Reputation In An Era Of Political Polarisation And Ai D 191Ed8C249
entry.summary: Securing brand trust and reputation in an era of political polarisation and AI-driven disinformation identifies generative AI as an additional mechanism that lets malicious actors disseminate increasingly realistic disinformation at unprecedented scale to inflict financial and reputational harm. This extends Kaal's engagement-driven Web2 misinformation mechanism with a content-generation amplifier. The abstract does not isolate platform architecture as the cause or measure distrust in legal institutions.

entry.title: Streaming Adversarial Auditing Multi Agent Detection Of Ai Generated Corporate Greenwashin 39Ea924081
entry.summary: Adversarial Auditing formulates AI-generated corporate-greenwashing detection as a three-player minimax game and reports theoretical analysis showing bounded training dynamics. This supplies a concrete theoretical adversarial-analysis method relevant to Kaal's resilience requirement. It does not replace testnet evidence against specified Sybil, collusion, or reputation-gaming participation levels.

entry.title: Streaming Context Engineering A Principal Agent Theory Of Ai Augmented Knowledge Work 178C754D12
entry.summary: Context Engineering: A Principal-Agent Theory of AI-Augmented Knowledge Work identifies costly, imperfectly observable, expertise-dependent context work as a mechanism creating moral hazard and screening problems inside firms. This extends Kaal's costly-monitoring account from ownership-control conflicts to human effort in AI-augmented knowledge work. The abstract does not establish that the same friction persists between artificial agents operating on fully attested substrates.

entry.title: Streaming Embedding Ethical Governance In Personal Ai Systems Design And Evaluation Of A U 270416F1Ac
entry.summary: Embedding ethical governance in personal AI systems states that personal AI can offer privacy and autonomy while shifting ethical, legal, and governance responsibility from organizations to individual users. This qualifies Kaal's individual-accountability design by identifying responsibility transfer as a burden as well as a governance mechanism. The abstract does not establish that individual allocation is fair, enforceable, or sufficient.

entry.title: Streaming Prac3 Privacy Reputation Accountability Consent Credit Compensation Voice Actors Cbe7D01Dbc
entry.summary: PRAC3 argues that consent, credit, and compensation frameworks do not adequately address voice-identity risks created when context, authorship, and control separate. This supplies a voice-data instance of multidimensional governance limits, extending Kaal's critique of unitary reputation scoring across privacy, regulation, and ethical change. The abstract does not evaluate DcentAI, WDAG, or a replacement scoring architecture.

entry.title: Streaming Separation Of Execution Optimization And Governance In Ai Agent Systems 01D595A91E
entry.summary: Separation of Execution, Optimization, and Governance in AI Agent Systems argues that conflating those functions creates self-reinforcing hallucinations, optimization drift, and forensically useless audit trails. This supplies a structural separation mechanism extending Kaal's warning about fragmented internal monitoring without external audit standards. It does not test Kaal's decentralized-governance design or show that separation alone resolves the failures.

entry.title: Streaming Reinforcement Learning Your Way Agent Characterization Through Policy Regulariza Ad45Bf1Af0
entry.summary: Reinforcement Learning Your Way states that the complexity of state-of-the-art reinforcement-learning algorithms produces opacity that inhibits explainability and understanding. This independently corresponds to Kaal's broader critique of current explainable RL. The abstract does not establish Kaal's more specific claims about toy examples, user testing, visualization complexity, or open-source practice.

entry.title: Streaming Aegis Agent Execution Governance And Integrity Standard A Survey And Reference A B8C0Fe8752
entry.summary: AEGIS reports a literature gap: no systematic academic framework for recording, verifying, and ensuring accountability for organizational AI-agent actions. This supplies a direct accountability gap to which Kaal's immutable decision-and-transaction record is a proposed design response. The abstract does not validate blockchain recording or prove that no other framework exists outside the reviewed scope.

entry.summary: Emergent Inter-Agent Conflict in Multi-Agent AI Systems identifies inter-agent objective divergence as a systems-level problem left largely outside human-AI alignment research. This extends Kaal's treatment of objective-function governance as a foundational policy problem into heterogeneous multi-agent interaction. The abstract proposition does not establish the frequency, severity, or institutional solution to divergence.

entry.title: Streaming Agent Based Trust And Reputation Model In Smart Iot Environments 4A9B10F9F7
entry.summary: Agent-Based Trust and Reputation Model in Smart IoT Environments states that open, dynamic IoT environments require collaboration with unknown entities that lack a proven track record. This supplies a distinct machine-to-machine setting in which missing performance history is operationally salient, extending Kaal's generative-exchange track-record mechanism. It does not test generative distributions or establish that reputation alone makes IoT collaboration trustworthy.

entry.title: Streaming Relational Integrity In Multi Agent Ai Systems A Polarity Model Framework For Hu 41D6938Fe0
entry.summary: Relational Integrity in Multi-Agent AI Systems argues that AI safety approaches which specify outcomes in advance become brittle when reality moves beyond the specification and can become sterile through over-constraint. This extends Kaal's brittleness mechanism for explicitly programmed legal expert systems to a broader AI-safety architecture setting. The abstract supplies an architectural claim, not a measured failure rate or evidence that every specified safety constraint is harmful.

entry.title: Streaming Performance Rather Than Reputation Affects Humans Trust Towards An Artificial Ag 8658A7Efae
entry.summary: Performance rather than Reputation Affects Humans' Trust towards an Artificial Agent reports that stated agent reputation changes self-reported trust before interaction. This qualifies Kaal's trustworthiness mechanism by separating perceived trust induced by a reputation cue from trustworthy behavior produced by validated contribution and reputation-weighted incentives. The experiment does not test that incentive mechanism or show that pre-interaction trust predicts performance.

entry.title: Streaming Bigdata Based University Reputation Measurement Towards Conceptualizing Ai Based 1209791E65
entry.summary: Bigdata-based university reputation measurement identifies electronic word of mouth as harder to measure, control, or influence than the factors used in traditional university rankings. This supplies a bounded university-reputation example of the objective-measurement difficulty in Kaal's reputation-governance claim. entry.title: Streaming Algorithmic Reputation Equivalence Are A Methodology For Developing Ai Decision Bcea8B299B
entry.summary: Algorithmic Reputation Equivalence reports that high human-perception reputation scores do not predict high AI decision-stage reputation scores and treats the two instruments as measuring categorically distinct phenomena. This provides a separate AI-facing example of why a single undifferentiated reputation measure can lose material information, extending Kaal's multidimensional-reputation requirement. It does not validate the WDAG design or transfer the brand-purchase result to dataset quality.

entry.title: Streaming Towards Secure Embodied Communication Management In Ai Era Reputation Guided Age 1B16Cd7Cd4

The abstract does not test SPoS or establish that reputation guidance resolves the attacks.
